rows.sourceTitle: Discoid lupus erythematosus and its progression to systemic lupus erythematosus across age groups: a systematic review
rows.citation: Alharbi A, Alamri O, Afandi A, Arbaeen A, Mirza A, Alahmari A, Alshomrani S, Qashqari M, Alahmadi M, Alharthy S, Kokandi A. Discoid lupus erythematosus and its progression to systemic lupus erythematosus across age groups: a systematic review. J Med Life. 2025;18(9):830-836. PMID 41178896. doi:10.25122/jml-2025-0141.
rows.proposition: Discoid lupus erythematosus can progress to systemic lupus erythematosus in a clinically meaningful subset of patients.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: established discoid lupus erythematosus with separately established systemic lupus erythematosus meeting appropriate classification/diagnostic criteria
rows.guard: Require established discoid lupus erythematosus and separately established systemic lupus erythematosus meeting appropriate classification or diagnostic criteria. Do not infer SLE from DLE alone. Preserve ANA and other autoantibody findings, hematologic abnormalities, systemic manifestations, family history, and other classification criteria as independent diagnostic evidence.
rows.scopeFinding: PubMed identity matches PMID/DOI/title. The systematic review reports progression from DLE to SLE in a clinically meaningful subset and therefore supports the implemented disease-progression proposition. The existing guard correctly requires separately established SLE rather than inferring systemic disease from DLE alone.

rows.sourceTitle: Functional outcomes of surgery for colon cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis
rows.citation: Verkuijl SJ, Jonker JE, Trzpis M, Burgerhof JGM, Broens PMA, Furnée EJB. Functional outcomes of surgery for colon cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur J Surg Oncol. 2021;47(5):960-969. PMID 33277056. doi:10.1016/j.ejso.2020.11.136.
rows.proposition: Fecal incontinence is a recognized long-term bowel-function complication after surgical treatment for colon cancer.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: colon cancer within the colorectal-cancer identity, actual bowel resection/colectomy, and separately documented fecal incontinence with compatible postoperative chronology
rows.guard: Require established colon cancer within the colorectal-cancer identity, actual colectomy or other bowel resection, and separately documented fecal incontinence with compatible postoperative chronology. Do not infer fecal incontinence from colorectal-cancer diagnosis alone, and do not generalize this colon-cancer surgical source to nonsurgical disease or rectal-cancer treatment without separate evidence. Preserve pre-existing continence disorders, neurologic disease, pelvic-floor dysfunction, inflammatory bowel disease, obstetric injury, medications, and other anorectal causes.
rows.scopeFinding: PubMed identity matches PMID/DOI/title. The meta-analysis directly quantifies bowel dysfunction, including liquid- and solid-stool incontinence, after colon-cancer surgery. The implemented guard properly restricts the broader colorectal-cancer identity to colon cancer with actual colectomy/bowel resection and compatible postoperative chronology.

rows.sourceTitle: Testosterone Therapy for Late-Onset Hypogonadism Improves Erectile Function: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.sourceDesign: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
rows.citation: Taniguchi H, Shimada S, Kinoshita H. Testosterone Therapy for Late-Onset Hypogonadism Improves Erectile Function: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Urol Int. 2022;106(6):539-552. PMID 34856556. doi:10.1159/000520135.
rows.proposition: Androgen-deficiency hypogonadism is clinically linked to impaired erectile function, and testosterone treatment in late-onset hypogonadism improves erectile-function scores at the population level.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: adult male androgen-deficiency hypogonadism consistent with the late-onset hypogonadism evidence and separately documented erectile dysfunction
rows.guard: Require established androgen-deficiency hypogonadism consistent with the source population, including late-onset hypogonadism when relying on this citation, and separately documented erectile dysfunction. Do not attribute every erectile-dysfunction case to hypogonadism. Preserve vascular and metabolic disease, diabetes, medication effects, neurologic disease, pelvic surgery, psychogenic factors, other endocrine disorders, and structural or urologic causes.
rows.scopeFinding: PubMed identity matches PMID/DOI/title. The systematic review/meta-analysis of randomized trials shows significantly improved erectile-function scores with testosterone therapy in late-onset hypogonadism. This supports the implemented population-level endocrine/functional relationship when limited to androgen-deficiency hypogonadism consistent with the source population; it does not establish that all erectile dysfunction is caused by hypogonadism.

rows.sourceTitle: Chronic Pancreatitis Is a Risk Factor for Pancreatic Cancer, and Incidence Increases With Duration of Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
rows.citation: Gandhi S, de la Fuente J, Murad MH, Majumder S. Chronic Pancreatitis Is a Risk Factor for Pancreatic Cancer, and Incidence Increases With Duration of Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Clin Transl Gastroenterol. 2022;13(3):e00463. PMID 35142721. doi:10.14309/ctg.0000000000000463.
rows.proposition: Chronic pancreatitis is associated with a substantially increased subsequent risk of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, with risk increasing with disease duration.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: chronic pancreatitis with separately established pancreatic cancer developing after the chronic-pancreatitis diagnosis with chronology that reduces reverse-causation risk
rows.guard: Primary phenotype must be chronic pancreatitis, not an isolated acute-pancreatitis episode. Require separately established pancreatic cancer and chronology compatible with cancer developing after chronic pancreatitis. Do not infer cancer from pancreatitis alone. Preserve hereditary syndromes, smoking, age, diabetes, obesity, alcohol exposure, other pancreatic-cancer risk factors, and the possibility that occult pancreatic cancer initially presented as pancreatitis.
rows.scopeFinding: PubMed identity matches PMID/DOI/title. The meta-analysis reports substantially increased PDAC risk in chronic pancreatitis, with elevated risk persisting in analyses excluding cancers diagnosed within two years of chronic-pancreatitis diagnosis. The implementation correctly restricts the generic pancreatitis identity to chronic pancreatitis and preserves reverse-causation and competing-risk guards.

rows.sourceTitle: Renal complications in patients with chronic hypoparathyroidism on conventional therapy: a systematic literature review : Renal disease in chronic hypoparathyroidism
rows.citation: Gosmanova EO, Houillier P, Rejnmark L, Marelli C, Bilezikian JP. Renal complications in patients with chronic hypoparathyroidism on conventional therapy: a systematic literature review: renal disease in chronic hypoparathyroidism. Rev Endocr Metab Disord. 2021;22(2):297-316. PMID 33599907. doi:10.1007/s11154-020-09613-1.
rows.proposition: Chronic hypoparathyroidism, particularly under long-term conventional calcium and active-vitamin-D therapy, is associated with increased renal complications including chronic kidney disease or renal insufficiency.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: chronic hypoparathyroidism with separately established chronic kidney disease; when conventional calcium/active-vitamin-D therapy is relied upon, documented treatment exposure and compatible chronology are required
rows.guard: Require chronic hypoparathyroidism and separately established chronic kidney disease. Where conventional calcium and active-vitamin-D therapy is relied upon as the pathway, require documented treatment exposure and compatible chronology. Preserve pre-existing CKD, diabetes, hypertension, recurrent acute kidney injury, nephrotoxic drugs, obstruction, nephrolithiasis or nephrocalcinosis, and other renal-disease causes.
rows.scopeFinding: PubMed identity matches PMID/DOI/title. The systematic review reports renal disease ranging from renal insufficiency to CKD in chronic hypoparathyroidism treated with oral calcium and active vitamin D. The implemented guard appropriately requires chronic hypoparathyroidism, separate CKD, and documented conventional-treatment exposure/chronology when that mechanism is relied upon.
